name: Elefsina
title: UTM Thickness Gauging in Elefsina: Shipyard & Anchorage
description: Ship UTM and thickness measurement in Elefsina bay at Skaramangas, Elefsis Shipyards or at anchor: renewal survey gauging and pre-docking steel estimates.
h1: Ship Thickness Measurement and Hull Gauging in Elefsina Bay
intro: The Bay of Elefsina, closed off by Salamina island just north-west of Piraeus, combines two of the largest shipyards in Greece with a sheltered anchorage where tankers wait for the refineries and idle ships lie for months. That mix produces some of the most demanding gauging in the region: older ships brought out of lay-up, heavy dockings at Skaramangas or Elefsis, and refinery-trade tankers checked between cargoes. We mobilise a team from India to the vessel, wherever it sits in the bay.

highlights.h: Two major yards on one bay
highlights.p: Skaramangas Shipyards on the eastern shore and Elefsis Shipyards at the head of the bay both take ships for docking and heavy repair, so one mobilisation can cover consecutive jobs in either yard.

The bay has long served as a lay-up ground. A ship reactivated after months idle needs its tanks, piping and steelwork checked before it trades again, and that is when a measured thickness picture matters most.

Crude and product tankers serving the refineries at Elefsina and Aspropyrgos often wait in the bay. Waiting time can go on deck, piping and ballast tank gauging without disturbing the cargo programme.

port.h: Elefsina bay: refinery tankers, lay-ups and heavy repair
p: Elefsina sits at the head of a nearly enclosed bay between the Attica mainland and Salamina, reached from the Saronic Gulf by channels at either end of the island. The shoreline is industrial: the HELLENiQ ENERGY refineries at Elefsina and Aspropyrgos, fuel and bulk terminals, the commercial port of Elefsina and two large shipyards. Most ships seen here are tankers working the refinery jetties, dry bulk ships serving local industry, and vessels waiting for orders, repair slots or a buyer in the sheltered water of the bay.

The bay's other identity is as an anchorage and lay-up ground. For decades owners have used its calm water to park ships out of employment, and ships held up by sales, disputes or financing have ended up here too. Wreck-removal efforts in recent years have cleared many of the abandoned hulks that once crowded the shallows, but the bay is still where ships wait. For inspection, that means a steady stream of reactivation and pre-sale work: owners and buyers who need to know what months of idleness have done to ballast tanks, piping and deck structure before a ship returns to service or changes hands.

The yards supply the heavy end of the market. Skaramangas, with its large dry dock, can take ships beyond the reach of the floating docks at nearby Perama, and Elefsis Shipyards handles docking and repair at the head of the bay. Large tankers and bulk carriers come here for renewal surveys that need extensive steel renewal, and that is where a gauging plan does most to keep a docking on schedule. Readings taken before arrival, or in the first days in dock, let the yard order plate, plan staging and allocate welders rather than discovering the scope plate by plate as tanks are opened. On older ships at their fourth or fifth renewal survey, the steel scope often is the docking programme.

facilities.h: Gauging locations around the Bay of Elefsina
p: Inside the yards, most work is renewal-survey and pre-docking gauging on older bulk carriers and tankers, done in the dock or alongside the repair quays. At the refinery jetties the windows are shorter and set by the cargo programme, so readings concentrate on main deck, deck piping and ballast spaces that can be entered safely during operations, subject to the terminal's permit-to-work rules. Ships at anchor or in lay-up are boarded by launch, and on a reactivation the first task is often confirming that spaces can be ventilated, tested and certified safe after a long period closed.

Elefsina also suits combined programmes. A fleet manager with one ship docking at Skaramangas and another waiting at anchor in the bay can have both gauged by the same team in one trip, and the Perama yards and the Piraeus anchorages are within easy reach by road. We plan such combined mobilisations so that the visa and travel arrangements cover the whole window, and so that the order of jobs follows the docking dates rather than the other way round. Where a laid-up ship is also being sold, the buyer's and seller's superintendents can attend the same gauging, which avoids a later argument over whose readings to trust.
list: Skaramangas Shipyards — dry-docking and heavy repair of large tankers and bulk carriers, with renewal-survey gauging of bottom, side shell, tanks and holds in the dry dock
Elefsis Shipyards — docking and repair at the head of the bay, including pre-docking and in-dock gauging for steel renewal planning
Refinery jetties at Elefsina and Aspropyrgos — deck plating, deck piping and accessible ballast tank gauging on tankers within terminal permit rules
Elefsina anchorage — ships waiting for orders, repair slots or sale, boarded by launch for condition, pre-purchase and pre-docking gauging
Lay-up moorings in the bay — reactivation gauging of ballast tanks, sea water and fire main piping, and deck structure after long idle periods
Commercial port of Elefsina — dry bulk and general cargo ships gauged during cargo operations by arrangement with the agent

context.h: Regulation and market context for ships in Elefsina bay
p: Ships in the bay are under Greek and EU rules. Port state control follows the Paris MoU, and the Mediterranean SOx emission control area that took effect on 1 May 2025 applies throughout the Saronic Gulf, so ships burn compliant low-sulphur fuel or rely on scrubbers. On a ship that has spent months in lay-up with its scrubber idle, the wash-water and overboard lines deserve a close look before reactivation: stagnant sea water and failed linings are a combination that thins pipe walls without obvious warning. EU ETS and FuelEU Maritime apply to voyages from here just as they do from Piraeus.

The market around Elefsina turns on decisions about older ships. An owner whose 20-year-old bulk carrier is due its fourth renewal survey must weigh the steel renewal it will need against the ship's remaining earning life; a buyer looking at a laid-up tanker needs to know whether the hull will support a CAP or vetting programme. Gauging done before the ship enters the yard gives both of them a defensible basis for that call. With most Greek ship managers a short drive away in Athens and Piraeus, the people taking the decision usually attend in person, and they expect readings presented by area so they can see where the steel is going.

jobs.h: Typical thickness gauging jobs in Elefsina
jobs.p: Elefsina work falls into three groups: heavy renewal-survey gauging in the two yards, short windows on tankers at the refinery jetties or at anchor, and condition gauging on ships coming out of lay-up or being sold. Each needs a different plan. Yard jobs are about volume and sequence, anchorage jobs about access and gas-freeing, and lay-up jobs about establishing safe entry before anything else.
list: Fourth renewal survey gauging on a Capesize bulk carrier in the Skaramangas dry dock, with transverse sections, hold frames and topside tanks measured so the yard can confirm steel renewal early.
Reactivation gauging on a product tanker after a long lay-up in the bay: ballast tanks, deck piping, fire main and sea water lines checked before the ship is offered for charter.
Pre-purchase gauging on a laid-up Supramax at the Elefsina anchorage, giving the buyer readings on hatch covers, hold plating and ballast tanks before an offer is firmed.
Pre-docking gauging on an Aframax tanker waiting off the Aspropyrgos jetties, to estimate deck and ballast tank renewal before it moves into a yard.
Magnetic particle crack detection at hatch corners and hopper knuckles on an older bulk carrier docking at Elefsis Shipyards, carried out alongside the hold gauging for its renewal survey.

logistics: The team flies into Athens International Airport and reaches the Elefsina shore by road. Entry to Skaramangas Shipyards, Elefsis Shipyards and the refinery terminals is controlled, so passes are applied for through the ship's agent with crew lists and technician certificates sent ahead; launches for ships at anchor or in lay-up are booked the same way. As Greece is a Schengen state, each technician travels on a Schengen visa obtained in India. For reactivations, where the date often hangs on a charter being fixed, we suggest starting the visa process once reactivation looks likely rather than when it is confirmed.

faqs.q: Can you gauge a ship that has been laid up in Elefsina bay for months?
faqs.a: Yes, but the first step is safe access rather than measurement. Tanks and voids that have been closed for a long time must be ventilated, tested and certified safe for entry by the ship's side before we go in. We then usually start with ballast tanks, deck and piping systems, which are the areas where long idleness does most harm, and extend the scope as the owner's plans become clear.

faqs.q: Is there time to gauge a tanker at the refinery jetties between cargo operations?
faqs.a: Sometimes, within limits. The terminal's safety rules restrict what can be done alongside, and cargo tanks are not available while loaded. Deck plating, deck piping and ballast tanks certified safe can often be gauged during the stay, and the remaining scope completed at anchor or in the yard. We agree the split with you and the terminal before the ship arrives.

faqs.q: Which yard in the bay should we choose for heavy steel renewal?
faqs.a: That is the owner's commercial decision, and we do not act for any yard. What we can provide is the pre-docking gauging that makes a comparison meaningful: a steel renewal estimate by area, based on measured readings rather than assumptions, which you can send to each yard you are considering, whether in the bay or at Perama.

faqs.q: Can one mobilisation cover a yard job and a ship at anchor?
faqs.a: Yes, if the windows overlap or follow each other closely. The bay is compact, the yards and the anchorage are reached from the same shore, and Perama and the Piraeus anchorages are close by road. Tell us every ship and date you have in mind, and we will plan one trip with visas valid for the whole period.
